old_title: Ukraine war latest: Trump 'not sure' about allowing Kyiv to build Patriot missiles
new_title: Ukraine war latest: Putin pounds Kyiv with ballistic missiles as nine dead
old_text:
US president Donald Trump said he was "not sure" he would let Ukraine build Patriot surface-to-air interceptor missiles.
"It's a very extraordinary weapon, and we have to be a little bit careful of who we licence to," the president said in his comments to FT yesterday. This comes weeks after offering to share the license of the coveted air defence systems with the war-hit nation.
On 10 July at the Nato summit in Ankara, Turkey, Trump said: "We'll give them the right to make Patriots. We'll show them how to do it," Trump said. "I think they can produce them pretty quickly."
Ukraine has been requesting the US for Patriot missiles to shoot down incoming Russian missiles, drones and bombs.
His remarks come just hours after Russia launched a North Korean ballistic missile at a Ukrainian village killing six members of a single family, president Volodymyr Zelensky said.
Ukrainian drones struck two more warehouses belonging to Russian online retailer Wildberries, sparking fires at both sites, the company and a regional official said on Thursday.
Ukraine strikes two more warehouses of Russian online retailer Wildberries
Ukrainian drones struck two more warehouses belonging to Russian online retailer Wildberries overnight, sparking fires at both sites, the company and a regional official said.
Ukraine has attacked about a dozen Wildberries sites since 18 July in a bid to disrupt the operations of the company, a linchpin of the consumer economy that is often described as Russia's answer to Amazon.
Oleg Melnichenko, governor of the Penza region in western Russia, said one person was injured and around 200 people were evacuated from the Wildberries site there.
Wildberries said a fire had also broken out at its logistics facility in Sarapul in Russia's Udmurtia region after a Ukrainian drone attack.
The company said staff had been evacuated in advance, that there were no preliminary reports of casualties, and that deliveries were being rerouted through other facilities.
Several Russian news outlets reported a third attack on a Wildberries site in the Urals region of Perm, but the company said its sorting centre there was operating normally.
Trump says he is 'not sure' on Ukraine building Patriot missiles - report
US president Donald Trump said he was "not sure" he would let Ukraine build Patriot missiles, The Financial Times reported on Thursday, citing a phone call with him.
Trump also said his envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff would visit Ukraine for the first time in the coming days, the Financial Times said.
"It's a very extraordinary weapon, and we have to be a little bit careful of who we licence to," the president said in his comments to FT.
Ukraine's envoy tells Washington 'we need the missiles'
Ukraine hopes a new push for ceasefire talks with Russia could halt the war before a potentially brutal winter, but needs new anti-ballistic missiles now to defend against strikes by Moscow, the country's envoy to Washington said.
Olha Stefanishyna told reporters that Ukraine was in discussions with the Pentagon about a license to produce Patriot PAC-3 missiles itself, but that process could take 12 months to five years.
"The devastating effect of every overnight attack right now is unbelievable," Stefanishyna said.
"Last night and the night before, it was 30 to 40 ballistic missiles."
While Ukraine was able to defend against Iranian and Russian-built drones, it had not yet developed an effective way to defend against ballistic missiles, whose production is being rapidly increased by Russian president Vladimir Putin.
"He has an intention to destroy Ukraine, and that's why, you know, we're looking for different capabilities. We have been successful in everything, but so far, for this winter, we need the missiles."
Discussions were also underway about Ukraine agreeing to a long-term purchase of PAC-3 missiles, and then swapping positions in the production line with another buyer.
Romania scrambles jets as aerial targets detected near Ukraine border
Romania, a member of European Union and Nato, briefly scrambled two fighter jets as a group of aerial targets was detected near its river border with Ukraine, the Romanian defence ministry said on social media website X.
The targets later disappeared from the radar monitoring systems without entering the national airspace, it said in a follow up post, adding that the air alert was lifted and explosions were reported on the Ukrainian territory.
Drone attack sparks fire at energy plant in Russia's Volgograd
A drone attack sparked a fire at an energy facility and warehouses in Russia's Volgograd region this morning, injuring five, the regional governor, Andrei Bocharov, said, but stopped short of giving details of the facility.
The region is home to a Lukoil-owned oil refinery.
At least five people are seeking medical help after the attacks, Bocharov added on Telegram.
In the neighbouring southern region of Rostov, a woman was injured after a drone attack in the town of Gukovo, regional governor Yuri Slyusar said on the messaging app.
Ukraine has recently stepped up attacks on Russian logistics hubs, such as those of top online retailer Wildberries, as it keeps up strikes on energy facilities that have triggered a supply crisis across most of Russia.
Wildberries, with a few of its warehouses hit as recently as Thursday, said on Telegram it had paid a second tranche of financial support to nearly 100,000 sellers whose goods were damaged.
Nato chief says Russian missile in Polish airspace 'reckless'
Nato officials said they have noted that Russian missile entered Polish airspace during the onslaught and landed in a rural area.
It caused no injuries or damage but could deepen tensions between the military alliance and Moscow, as wary European countries fear the 4-year-old war could spill into their territory.
Nato secretary-general Mark Rutte called it "yet another reckless act by Russia and a dangerous consequence of its war against Ukraine."
Polish prime minister Donald Tusk said it was "a very serious incident," but added: "There are absolutely no reasons to believe that Poland was the target."
'Scared' British tourist in Poland films moment air raid sirens sound during Russian strikes in Ukraine
A British tourist in Poland has captured on camera the moment air raid sirens started blaring during Russian strikes in Ukraine.
In the early hours of Thursday, Ryan, who was staying in Lublin, was woken to the sounds of sirens.
"As a British tourist this scared the hell out of me," he wrote.
The alarm was triggered by Russian airstrikes in neighbouring Ukraine, which killed eight people. The sirens stopped after a few minutes.
Poland's defence minister Wladyslav Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the country endured an "extremely tough night", which saw sirens blare, F-16 fighter jets scrambled and a suspected Russian missile crash into a field.
Russia says it hit vessel with military cargo near Ukraine's Odesa
Russian forces struck a vessel carrying military cargo near Ukraine's Odesa, the Russian defence ministry said this morning.
Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks in recent weeks on ships that they say are aiding the other side's war effort.
Russia extends diesel and gasoline export bans until end of January 2027
The Russian government extended its bans on the export of diesel and gasoline until 31 January, 2027, it said in a statement on Thursday.
Russia initially introduced the ban on diesel from 8 July to 31 July as part of a broader package of measures to support the domestic fuel market after repeated Ukrainian drone attacks on oil refineries triggered fuel shortages and price spikes.
Moscow had already imposed restrictions on exports of gasoline and jet fuel.
North Korean missile likely used in Russian strike that killed five family members
A Russian overnight assault that tragically claimed the lives of a family near the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih is believed to have involved a North Korean missile, according to two sources. This marks the first suspected use of such a weapon in the conflict for almost a year.
While Russia has previously deployed North Korean missiles against Ukrainian targets, their re-emergence after a significant hiatus suggests Moscow has replenished its arsenal. This fresh stock of weapons could enable Russia to escalate its missile campaign against its neighbour, one source indicated.
The military source, who requested anonymity due to the sensitivity of the information, said August 8, 2025 was the last time that Ukraine confirmed a Russian strike using a North Korean missile. Russia began firing North Korean KN-23 and KN-24 short-range ballistic missiles at Ukraine towards the end of 2023.

Russia pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles, killing at least nine people and injuring 28 others in the second such intense barrage in a week.
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said a residential building in the Shevchenkivskyi district was partially destroyed, trapping people inside. The first and second floors of the building partially collapsed.
More than a dozen explosions rocked the Ukrainian capital, sparking fires across the city and causing power outages in some areas.
The assault came just a week after a similar attack killed nine people, including six members of one family, among them children.
The latest strike came as US president Donald Trump said he was "not sure" he would allow Ukraine to build Patriot surface-to-air interceptor missiles under licence, casting doubt on Kyiv's hopes of reducing its reliance on Washington for critical air defences.
"It's a very extraordinary weapon, and we have to be a little bit careful of who we license to," the president told the Financial Times on Thursday, weeks after offering to share the production licence for the coveted air defence system with the war-hit nation.
Ukraine has repeatedly asked the US for Patriot missile systems to help intercept Russian missiles, drones and aerial bombs.
Zelensky asks Elon Musk to allow Starlink-assisted strikes on Russia
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday urged Donald Trump and other US officials to help secure permission from Elon Musk to use Starlink satellite internet services to guide strikes inside Russia.
According to a person familiar with the matter, Zelensky made the request directly to Trump during their Oval Office meeting this week.
He also raised the issue with lawmakers on Capitol Hill, seeking Starlink's support.
Trump did not commit to the request.
While Musk allows Starlink to operate across Ukraine, including Russian-occupied territories, access remains restricted inside Russia.
Zelensky says Patriot interceptors remain top priority in call with Vance
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky said he held a "good" phone call with US vice president JD Vance, with air defence remaining a top priority as Russia's attacks continue.
Zelensky said the two discussed the urgent need for Patriot interceptors to defend against ballistic missiles, followed up on his recent meeting with president Donald Trump in Washington.
"As Russia's air attacks on our country continue unabated, air defence - specifically Patriot interceptors against ballistic missiles - remains a top priority," he said.
"The Vice President and I also spoke about the consequences of Russia's war for global markets."
He said both sides agreed to keep their teams in close contact and thanked the US for its continued support.
Pictures show aftermath of Russian strikes in Kyiv
Rescuers have been working to douse the flames after multiple multi-storey residential buildings caught fire in a major Russian air attack on Kyiv this morning.
Pictures from the Ukrainian capital show a huge crater near a children's clinic following an attack that included multiple Russian ballistic missiles.
Death toll rises to nine in Kyiv strikes
Russia pounded Ukraine's capital Kyiv with ballistic missiles on Saturday, killing at least nine people and wounding 28 others, including four children, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
Klitschko said a residential building in Shevchenkivskyi district was partially destroyed, trapping people inside.
The first and second floors of the damaged building had partially collapsed, he said.Some warehouses were also on fire, he said.
Russia has stepped up attacks on the capital in recent months, while Ukraine is chronically short of air defences capable of downing ballistic missiles, which travel at several times the speed of sound.
This is the second major attack on Kyiv this week.
The attack on Thursday killed nine people, including six members of one family in a village near Kryvyi Rih. In Kyiv, fires broke out across the city and power outages were reported in some areas.
Russia 'using Ceuta crisis to sow destabilisation' across Europe
Ukraine has accused Russia of carrying out an "intensive propaganda campaign" using pictures from Ceuta to "sow destabilisation".
Foreign minister Andrii Sybiha claimed that Ukrainian analysts have identified more than 1,500 publications on a pro-Russian network, led by Pravda and RT.
"For years, Moscow has used migration and other sensitive topics to stoke fear and destabilise European countries," he wrote on X.
Three dead as Russia pounds Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones
At least three people were killed and over a dozen others injured after Russia launched an intense barrage of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Kyiv overnight into Saturday, local authorities said.
A five-story residential building in the Solomianskyi District was damaged by falling debris with people believed to be still trapped inside and a fire in the courtyard, said Kyiv mayor Vitalii Klitschko in a post on Telegram.
People were also reportedly trapped in another residential building the Shevchenkivskyi district, after a partial collapse on the first and second floors, Klitschko said.
Elsewhere in the capital, warehouse buildings were on fire in the Darnytskyi district, he said.
The attack came just two days after a large-scale Russian ballistic missile and drone attack across Ukraine killed 10 civilians and wounded more than 50 others and saw a Russian missile enter Polish airspace.
Recap: Romania briefly scrambles jets as aerial targets detected near Ukraine border
Nato member Romania briefly scrambled two fighter jets as a group of aerial targets was detected near its river border with Ukraine, the Romanian Defence Ministry said on Friday.
The targets later disappeared from the radar monitoring systems without entering the national airspace, it said in a follow up post, adding that the air alert was lifted and explosions were reported on the Ukrainian territory.
